conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Lee. You're here today for your scheduled left lower extremity angiogram, correct?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, that's right. I’ve been waiting for this since my last hospital stay.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. Last time, the procedure was postponed because of kidney concerns. But now we’ve optimized your condition, so we’re going ahead today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. My foot ulcer hasn’t been healing, and I’m worried about it getting worse.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s exactly why we’re doing the angiogram — to check the blood flow to your leg and foot. Poor circulation can delay healing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will they fix anything during the test?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Sometimes they can do both, but today the main goal is diagnosis. If there’s a blockage that can be treated, they might, but we’ll see what the images show.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. And I heard they’re using the groin to access the artery?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, they’ll go through the right femoral artery. It’s a common approach. You’ll be sedated, so you won’t feel much.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my warfarin? I stopped it before coming, like last time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, that was correct. We’re not giving it today, but you’ll restart it tomorrow night after we make sure there’s no bleeding risk.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Alright. And my other meds — should I take them?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Most will be resumed after the procedure. Things like your aspirin, statin, and torsemide. We’ll hold anything that might affect bleeding until we’re sure you’re stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, thanks. I just want to make sure everything’s covered.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Absolutely. We’ll monitor you closely. Any signs of pain, swelling, or numbness after the procedure, let us know right away.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi again. You did well during the angiogram. They accessed the right femoral artery and looked at the left leg’s blood vessels.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And what did they find?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The main arteries in your thigh are open, but there are a few narrow spots that aren’t severe. The bigger issue is in the lower leg.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What’s going on down there?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The posterior tibial artery is completely blocked. That’s one of the two main arteries to the foot. The anterior tibial is open and reaches the forefoot, but the hindfoot isn’t getting good blood flow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So that’s why my heel ulcer isn’t healing?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Without enough blood, wounds can’t heal properly. Given the findings, they decided not to do any intervention today — it wouldn’t help much with the current blockage pattern.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So what now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We focus on wound care and managing your other conditions. You’ll keep using the honey gel and ammonium lactate. Good blood sugar control is also key.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: My sugars have been hard to control with the gastroparesis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I know. That’s why we’re continuing the sliding scale insulin. We’ll check your levels regularly and adjust as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my kidneys? Last time they were worried about contrast affecting them.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good point. They used minimal contrast and took precautions. Your creatinine is 2.2, which is stable for you, so no acute kidney injury.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. You’re doing well. Vital signs are stable, and you’ve been eating and moving around without issues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel okay. A little tired, but no pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s expected. The procedure takes energy, even if you were sedated. Your foot and groin site are looking good — no swelling or bleeding.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Can I go home today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we think you’re ready. You’ll go home with instructions on wound care, activity, and when to call us if something goes wrong.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my warfarin?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll restart your 4 mg dose tonight. Just like before. Keep an eye on the groin site — if it starts bleeding or swells, lie down and press on it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And when do I follow up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll have an appointment for bilateral ABI/PVR tests to monitor blood flow. The office will call you to schedule.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, thank you. I’ll keep my foot elevated and take care of the ulcer.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. And watch for any new pain, coldness, or color changes in your leg. Call us if those happen, or if you get a fever over 101.5.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks for explaining everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. We’ll get your discharge papers ready, and you should be out within the hour.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just a quick check before you leave — any questions about your meds or wound care?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, it’s all clear. I’ll keep using the honey gel every other day and the ammonium lactate daily.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. And remember — no heavy lifting for a week, and don’t drive while on pain meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. I’ll have my daughter help with chores.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s a good plan. Take care, and we’ll see you in follow-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Have a safe trip home.
